title: Tub Transfer Benches and Shower Seats: What to Measure Before You Buy
subtitle: A transfer bench is meant for people who find the tub wall the hard part, but only if it fits your tub and the person using it.
excerpt: If stepping over a high tub wall feels risky, a tub transfer bench may help. Here is what to measure and two options from $84.99 (Home Depot price, November 2026).
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: For many people, the riskiest moment of the day is getting into the bathtub. You have to lift one leg over a high wall while balancing on the other, often on a wet, slippery surface. Getting out again is no easier.

A tub transfer bench is meant for that problem. Instead of stepping over the edge, the seat slides across the tub edge. This guide explains the difference between benches and shower chairs, what they cannot do and what to measure before you order one. We have not tested any product here. Specs and prices come from the Home Depot product pages.
A regular shower chair sits entirely inside the tub or shower. An occupational therapist's guide from the Mayo Clinic store puts it simply:
"A shower chair is usually best for a walk-in shower with little or no threshold." (Mayo Clinic store, An Occupational Therapist's Guide to Preventing Falls in the Bathroom)

In short, a chair suits someone who can step in safely but should sit while washing. If stepping over the tub wall is the hard part, a transfer bench, where the seat slides across the tub edge, is usually the better type.

Be clear about the limits. A seat does not lower the tub wall, and it is not a commode or a rolling shower chair. It is not right for someone who needs help being lifted. If stepping over is unsafe, ask your doctor about an occupational therapist, a specialist who helps people manage daily tasks safely. In some homes, a walk-in shower may be needed.

items: Measure three things first: the height of the tub edge, the inside width of the tub, and the space beside the tub for a transfer bench.
Check the leg range. For example, legs that adjust from 16 to 20 inches only fit certain tub-edge heights.
Know the weight limit. Look for a stated capacity. If a product page does not list one, ask the seller before buying, and choose a higher-capacity model for a heavier user.

Look at the feet. Suction feet rely on a smooth, clean tub surface, so non-slip feet are the safer bet on textured tubs. One buyer's guide, The Consumer's Guide (a review site, not a lab test), also ranks weighted suction-cup designs lower for this reason.
Left or right? Check that the product says it fits your tub. The Glacier Bay below says it adjusts to fit both left and right bathtubs.
Backrest: a backrest may add support while seated. Check whether it is included or removable.
Budget for a hand-held shower head. A seat works best with one, and neither product page says whether one is included.

Price and returns: both prices below are one-time, with no fee or subscription shown. Both pages list 90-day returns, in store or online. The card offers require opening a new Home Depot credit card, so check the terms before applying.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well
Follow the maker's assembly instructions. The Glacier Bay page does not give assembly details in the notes we have, and the Drive page lists none, so ask the seller what is included before you buy.
As general guidance, not from the product pages: have a helper nearby the first few times, and ask an occupational therapist how to get on and off safely.

Mayo Clinic's fall-prevention advice (mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/healthy-aging/in-depth/fall-prevention/art-20047358) also recommends non-slip mats in the tub or shower, and a sturdy plastic seat with a hand-held nozzle.

A seat makes bathing easier to manage, but it cannot prevent every slip or fall. It is not a medical alert device, and it does not replace advice from your doctor or an occupational therapist. The Drive page states no weight capacity, which matters for a seat people put their full weight on, so get a written capacity from the seller before buying.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: A little measuring now saves a frustrating return later. Get the right fit, and bath time can go back to being something to look forward to.
